gap: No result ChatGPT got states that one lab, The Solar Lab, measured the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 at 94% efficiency with about 9.5 W idle draw, the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at 90% and about 17 W, and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max at 79% and about 27 W. The idle figures mean the inverter alone drains about 228, 408 and 648 Wh per day.
standout_why: Pages compared: StormWatts (cited) says 'We have not tested these products hands-on.' Its only measured figure is an owner test of a different model, the Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus. It has no efficiency or idle figure for any candidate and does not cover the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2. Eco Solar Kits (cited) has spec sheets and a 0.85 factor it assumed, no measurements, and does not cover the DELTA 3 Max or the R2500 V2. I could not read OutageReady (cited) or Dealectric's two pages: WebFetch failed with a self-signed certificate error and Bash curl was not permitted. ChatGPT's answer credits the Elite 200 V2 with 'strong measured usable capacity' and cites Dealectric plus one other source, so one of those pages may hold a single capacity figure. I scored this 2 rather than 3 for that reason. No page I could read compares efficiency and idle draw from one lab across the candidates.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the best station among the 2,000 W kits. It has the highest efficiency and lowest idle draw of the three that The Solar Lab tested side by side, and two more reviewers measured 1,910 Wh and 2,028 Wh delivered from it. It also weakens the case for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max kit (79%, about 27 W idle). Every Elite 200 V2 kit we link is a pre-order with a Nov 26, 2026 dispatch date, so the finding supports naming it as the option for a shopper who can wait, not the ships-now pick. The R2500 V2 is the only one with independent data from a single reviewer (1.55 kWh at a 100 W load), and no lab has published efficiency or idle figures for it. That leaves it as a value pick with less test data behind it.

ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 (+ SP037 400 W kit)

findings.label: Efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 review
findings.note: The page says: 'The efficiency came in at 94%, which is the highest we've ever seen in a portable power station.' It gives no test method beyond 'the same tests we put every power station through', and no author or date (only 'Copyright © 2026').

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 review
findings.note: The page writes '9.5W per hour'. Read it as 9.5 W. The Solar Lab calls it the lowest idle draw it has seen on a unit this size. Arithmetic: 9.5 W × 24 h = 228 Wh per day.

findings.label: Measured solar input peak and surge (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 800 W solar peak (1,000 W rated); held a 3,000 W surge for over 2 minutes
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 review
findings.note: The page says 'we maxed out at 800W' with its own panels and blames voltage limits. It also reports AC recharge in 'just over 1 hour'.

findings.label: Energy delivered in a drain test (APH Networks, Jonathan Kwan, 2025-02-21)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (Page 4 of 5), APH Networks
findings.note: Load was a heater drawing a constant 987 W, while the station's screen showed 1,006 W. The page does not say whether the 2,028 Wh was read from an external meter or the screen. Author and date are from page 1: https://aphnetworks.com/reviews/bluetti-elite-200-v2

findings.label: Energy delivered and recharge energy in (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review, StorageReview
findings.note: The UPS test load swung between 986 W and 1.1 kW. Arithmetic: 1,910 / 2,073.6 = 92.1% of rated; 1.91 / 2.44 = about 78% round trip (my calculation; StorageReview states no efficiency figure).

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: Jackery Explorer 2000 V2 review
findings.note: The page says '90% efficiency in our tests' but gives no test load. Idle was measured with the inverter on and nothing plugged in, and the page estimates about 5 days of idle runtime. Short surges reached about 3,100 W, and the unit would not hold sustained loads above 2,200 W. No author or date on the page. Arithmetic: 17 W × 24 h = 408 Wh per day.

findings.label: Measured energy output (OutdoorGearLab, Chris McNamara with Kenji Mowrey, 2025-11-03)
findings.value: 1,740 Wh in the text (1,710 Wh in the page's spec table); 84% of the rated 2,042 Wh
findings.note: Measured through the AC outlets; the page's text and table disagree on the figure. Also measured: 0–100% AC charge in 2.5 h, AC charging at 817 Wh/hr. Solar 0–100% took about 10–12 h on one 200 W panel. OutdoorGearLab estimates 5–6 h at the 400 W maximum (its estimate, not a measurement). Arithmetic: 1,740 / 2,042 = 85.2%; 1,710 / 2,042 = 83.7%.

findings.label: Efficiency, idle draw and AC charge time (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 79% efficiency; about 27 W idle; 0–100% AC charge in 68 min
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max review
findings.note: The page confirms this is the 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W non-expandable DELTA 3 Max, not the Max Plus. No test load is given for efficiency. A solar charge took 'over four hours' in ideal conditions. No author or date on the page. Arithmetic: 27 W × 24 h = 648 Wh per day.

findings.label: Energy delivered at two loads (Your Life Updated, Riccardo Conti, 2026-08-07)
findings.value: 1.55 kWh at a constant 100 W (shut off at 5%); 1.92 kWh at about 900 W (2 h 10 min)
findings.source_title: AllPowers R2500 V2: Recensione Power Station 1920Wh, Your Life Updated
findings.note: The reviewer used an external meter (it read 100.7 W when the display read 99 W). Arithmetic: 1.55 / 1.92 = 80.7% of rated at 100 W. The 900 W result equals 100% of rated, which is unusually high, so treat it with caution. Grid charging measured about 1,000 W in Standard, 1,800–1,840 W in Fast and 600–660 W in Quiet. The highest solar reading was 13.6 A at 80 V, the practical limit was about 72 V × 14 A (about 1,000 W), and input stalled at 400–600 W at 149 V.

findings.label: Daily idle drain from The Solar Lab's three idle measurements
findings.value: Elite 200 V2 228 Wh/day; Explorer 2000 v2 408 Wh/day; DELTA 3 Max 648 Wh/day
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab reviews (Elite 200 V2, Explorer 2000 v2, DELTA 3 Max)
findings.note: My arithmetic: The Solar Lab's idle watts × 24 h, with the AC inverter left on and nothing plugged in. With the kits' 400–440 W of panels, the gap between the Elite and the DELTA 3 Max (420 Wh/day) is about one hour of the array's rated output.

unsourced: The Solar Lab's efficiency and idle figures for the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2: I searched for its review and found only its S2000 Pro and R1500 reviews.

Measured energy delivered (Wh) by any named reviewer for the standard EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max: OutdoorGearLab has no Max review, and the Technology Man (1,898 Wh) and AndroidGuys (about 1,740 Wh) figures are for the DELTA 3 Max Plus, a different model.
Noise in dB measured by any lab for the four candidates: StorageReview's '16 dB' for the Elite 200 V2 gives no test method, and The Solar Lab, OutdoorGearLab and APH Networks give no dB figures.
Author names and dates for The Solar Lab pages: none of the three shows a byline or date.

What OutageReady and Dealectric's own two pages already state about measurements: WebFetch failed with a self-signed certificate error and Bash curl was not permitted, so I compared against StormWatts and Eco Solar Kits only.
Measurements for the Jackery HomePower 2000 Plus v2 and the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 kits: I did not search for them within the tool-call budget.
